newsitem.title: PERU: Dead officer leaves farewell card before Peru raid.
newsitem.headline: Dead officer leaves farewell card before Peru raid.

text.p: A Peruvian naval commando who died in Tuesday's hostage rescue at the Japanese ambassador's home left a farewell note for the men he led on the mission.

"To my men: If you read this letter it is because I have died," Juan Valer wrote, local media reported on Thursday. "Think that I am at peace and the only thing I want is that people say Valer was a good man."

Seven bullets struck Valer as he was leading Peruvian Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela -- the Tupac Amaru guerrillas' prize captive -- to safety across the mansion's roof amid a hail of gunfire and grenade explosions.
With a handpicked group of elite troops, Valer stormed the upper-floor room where the rebels guarded their key hostages and dragged Tudela, who was shot in the ankle, out of the building.
Valer, 38, the father of two young girls, "loved his force as much as his family," his mother Aurora Sandoval said.

A bodyguard of President Alberti Fujimori's son Kenji, Valer was one of the two commandos who died in the dramatic assault. All 14 of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels and one of the 72 captives, Supreme Court judge Carlos Giusti, also died in the raid.
